Heard Mr. Durgesh Kumar Singh, the learned counsel for revisionists, the learned A.G.A. for State-opposite party 1 and Mr. S.S. Sharma, the learned counsel representing opposite party 2.

This criminal revision has been filed challenging the order dated 29.03.2023, passed by Additional Sessions Judge (Fast Track/Crime against Women), Mathura in Sessions Trial No.28220 of 2022 (State Vs. Puneet Dhatre and others), arising out of Case Crime No.67 of 2022, under Sections 354,

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When confronted with above, the learned counsel for revisionists contends that he does not dispute the submissions urged by the learned counsel for opposite party 2.

However, the interest of justice shall be served in case an observation is made by this Court that it shall be open for the revisionists to raise all legal pleas in support of their defense at the time of final hearing before the court below.
Learned A.G.A. for State and the learned counsel representing opposite party 2 have no objection to the same.
In view of above, prayer prayed for by means of present criminal revision is refused.
However, it is observed that it shall be open to the revisionists to raise all legal pleas available to them in opposition of the charges framed against them at the time of final hearing.
With the aforesaid direction/observation, this criminal revision stands disposed off.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
At the very outset, the learned counsel for first informant-opposite party 2 submits that charges have been framed against revisionist on 31.05.2023 therefore by reason of above and also the law laid down by the Apex Court in Ratilal Bhanji Mithani Vs. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for revisionists contends that he does not dispute the submissions urged by the learned counsel for opposite party 2.
